newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreigners buy $56 mln Jordan stocks in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners buy $56 mln Jordan stocks in H1 1997.

text.p: Non-Jordanian investors, both global funds and Arabs, bought an unprecedented 39.5 million dinars ($56 million) worth of Amman listed stocks in the first half of 1997, official bourse data released on Friday showed.

The figures breakdown for the January-June period show that global emerging funds purchases reached 57 percent of the total amount worth 22.4 million dinars while the rest was bought by Arab investors.
This compares with total international fund buying in the whole of 1996 which did not not exceed 9.6 million dinars ($13.5 million).
Non-Jordanian purchases on listed shares in the Amman Financial Market also rose in June to 15.4 million dinars against to 11.6 million dinars the previous month.
However Arab investor demand in June surpassed global funds by 20 percent in buying orders worth 8.4 million dinars compared to seven million dinars purchased by global funds.
"Last June was characterised by an increase in the activity and interest by Arab investors in buying Jordanian stock," said Wahib Shair, head of the Amman Financial Market.
This is partly attributed to mainly Kuwaiti investors who went on a buying spree on Jordan-Kuwait Bank JOBK.AM stock, helping to raise their equity stake close to 50 percent.
Much of the total international demand has surfaced since the second half of May after a roadshow in London focused on available investment opportunities on key Jordanian blue-chips.
Global funds' stake on the bourse stood at end of 1996 at just 1.5 percent of a total market capitalisation of 3.5 billion dinars against a 33 percent held by non-Jordanian Arab investors.
The rest is held by the government and Jordanian investors.
